claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine whether you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to gather some information about you and your children.

Let me start with a basic question:

**How many children are you inquiring about, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm inquiring about my son Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So I'm helping you determine eligibility for Child Benefit for your son **Alex**.

To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you some questions about your circumstances. Let me start:

**What is Alex's date of birth?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's 14 years old - born in January 2011.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. So Alex was born in January 2011, making him 14 years old.

**Are you Alex's parent or guardian, and do you have parental responsibility for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm his parent and I have parental responsibility for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good, thank you for confirming that.

**Are you currently living in the UK, and if so, what is your residency status?** (For example, are you a British citizen, settled status, visa holder, etc.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, no - I don't currently live in the UK. I'm living abroad at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. That's important information.

**Does Alex currently live in the UK, or is he also living abroad with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's living abroad with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. Thank you for that information.

**Are you a British citizen, or do you have any of the following: settled status in the UK, a visa that grants you the right to reside in the UK, or citizenship of an EEA country?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I am a British citizen, yes.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that you're a British citizen.

**Which country are you currently living in with Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: We're currently living in Spain.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

**Are you working or paying National Insurance contributions in the UK, or do you have any connection to the UK social security system (such as being posted abroad by a UK employer)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not working in the UK or paying National Insurance there. We've just relocated here - no connection to the UK social security system at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification.

**Do you intend to return to the UK to live, or is this move to Spain permanent at this stage?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: We're planning to stay in Spain for the foreseeable future - it's not just a temporary thing.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I appreciate you providing that information. Let me ask one more important question to complete my assessment:

**Since you're living abroad and not working in the UK, are you receiving any UK state benefits currently, or have you claimed any UK benefits in the past that might still be relevant to your situation?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not receiving any UK state benefits currently.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for answering all of my questions. I now have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me carefully consider the rules based on your circumstances:

- You are a British citizen
- You are living abroad in Spain with your son Alex (who is 14 years old)
- You are not working in the UK or paying National Insurance contributions
- You have no connection to the UK social security system
- You are not receiving any UK state benefits
- You intend to stay in Spain for the foreseeable future

Based on the Child Benefit eligibility rules, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex** at this time. The key reason is that Child Benefit is only payable to people who are living in the UK or in specific circumstances abroad (such as being posted abroad by a UK employer, or having certain employment/social security connections to the UK). Since you are living permanently abroad in Spain with no current work or social security connection to the UK, you do not meet the residency requirements for Child Benefit eligibility.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Your eligibility outcome:**

Unfortunately, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex** at this time.

The main reason is the residency requirement. While you are a British citizen and have parental responsibility for Alex, Child Benefit is primarily designed for those living in the UK. Although there are some exceptions that allow people to claim from abroad in limited circumstances (such as if you were posted abroad by a UK employer), your situation doesn't fall into those exceptions since you are permanently relocating to Spain with no qualifying UK work or social security connection.

If your circumstances change in the future—for example, if you return to live in the UK—you may become eligible to claim Child Benefit at that point.
